title: Autoscale Fabric: Terraform bridge for GPU node groups and ASG/Karpenter in Private VPC
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Summary: Build a reusable Terraform module (autoscale-fabric/gpu) that acts as a thin orchestration layer to provision GPU node groups inside Private VPCs and wire them to either ASG-backed or Karpenter-backed autoscaling. The module must support driver/AMI bootstrapping, mixed instance/spot pools, healthcheck probes for node readiness, seamless in-place upgrades, and safe fallback to lower-cost instance types when capacity is constrained.

Goals:
- Provide a single Terraform interface that teams can use to create GPU capacity for Private deployments with predictable networking and IAM defaults.
- Allow operator-configurable policies: prefer-spot, spot-fallback-to-on-demand, max-unavailable during upgrades, and k8s taints/labels templates.
- Support two runtime modes: classic ASG mode and dynamic Karpenter mode. Switching modes should be a flag without destructive replacement when possible.
- Implement health checks: node-launch-liveness (NLL) probe based on kubelet + NVIDIA driver install, and a runtime GPU-sanity check that verifies NVML visibility and container runtime GPU passthrough.
- Upgrade flow: support safe AMI/driver rollouts using rolling update windows, node cordon/drain hooks, and canary node groups.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Module has stable variables documented and examples for both ASG and Karpenter flows.
- Module can create a mixed-instance GPU pool with spot fallback policy and attach to existing VPC subnets and SGs.
- Healthcheck scripts run on boot and report to a node-provisioning S3 bucket + CloudWatch logs (customer-controlled).
- Terraform plan for a mode toggle (ASG <-> Karpenter) does not destroy production workloads in the default scenario documented.
- End-to-end manual validation run in staging: create cluster -> provision GPU pool -> schedule test workload -> simulate driver upgrade -> observe <5% job failures and roll forward.

Design notes and important trade-offs:
- Module will not attempt to fully manage the EKS cluster resource; it will assume an existing cluster and accept cluster_name and oidc provider ARNs. This reduces blast radius and keeps responsibilities separate between cluster lifecycle and GPU capacity provisioning.
- For ASG path we will use launch templates with user-data that invokes our node-bootstrapper (internal repo link below). For Karpenter path we emit NodeTemplate/Provisioner CRD fragments and IAM role bindings.
- Spot instances are cheaper but unpredictable. We provide a policy variable spot_preference (always|prefer|never) and implement a documented fallback hook that will create a small on-demand buffer pool to absorb evictions. This avoids mass rebuilds and keeps latency SLOs for inference customers.
- Healthchecks run on a local systemd timer to allow early failure detection before joining k8s; this prevents nodes that silently fail GPU init from entering the scheduler.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Module scaffolding + variables + docs examples (ASG & Karpenter) (2d)
2) Launch template & bootstrap user-data integration with driver install (3d)
3) Spot fallback and mixed instance configs, tests in staging (3d)
4) Healthcheck scripts + CloudWatch/S3 artifacts (2d)
5) Safe upgrade flow: canary nodegroup + rolling drain automation (2d)
6) QA runbook and run in staging; perf/latency tests with sample workloads (4d)

Observability and runbooks:
- The module will emit CloudWatch metrics and a small helper Lambda (optional) that aggregates node bootstrap failures and sends to the Console's ingestion endpoint. We will include a runbook: how to read bootstrap failure artifacts, how to kick a manual fallback, and how to pin a nodegroup to an AMI.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/private/gpu-autoscale-fabric (internal)
- Bootstrapper repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-bootstrapper/pull/178 (internal PR)
- Example TF usage: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/gpu-terraform-examples (internal)
- Staging test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/gpu-provisioning/staging-pools (internal)

notes: Testing checklist: terraform plan/apply in a disposable staging account; verify kube nodes appear and export nvidia-smi from a debug pod; simulate spot interruptions and observe fallback behavior; run driver upgrade by baking new AMI and follow rolling update playbook.

Rollback plan: pin workload tolerations to older nodegroups and scale down the new pool; if launch template change causes issues, revert to previous launch template version via TF state import and apply.

Known risk: switching from ASG to Karpenter may require IAM role mapping and minor downtime for controller reconciliation. We aim to document the safe sequence and provide an automated pre-check script.

Compatibility note: This module will support the two common AWS patterns we run: AL2+NVIDIA drivers with containerd and Ubuntu GPU AMIs. We will include example variables for DriverVersion and ContainerRuntime.
Metrics to track: node_bootstrap_failures, gpu_visibility_failures, average_time_to_ready, spot_eviction_rate, percent_capacity_fallbacked.
